openings.claim: Probe two opposed, padded, removable strip-pair clamps with lateral bearing stops; separation retention and position control use different contacts.
openings.delta: Replace dependence on seal friction with strip edges or bolt shafts bearing against hatch edges. Upper strips retain separation with balanced, modest preload. Tether removable hardware and park clamps outside the opening before inspection. The nearest rival is the same padded assembly retaining the hatch through compression and friction alone.
openings.prediction: If stops carry the sideways load, reducing preload while retaining capture should preserve position under 20 N without reproducing the opposite-corner lift. The friction rival should slide more under equivalent low preload. These are hypotheses, including reopening within 30 seconds and survival of the right-contact card.
openings.probe: First check rim underside access, strip reach, bolt length, and recoverable parking; fabricate only if these permit reversible capture without touching the seal destructively. Allocate twelve closure/pull trials: one disturbed low-preload friction-rival trial, ten candidate opening cycles with closure/pull checks, then one disturbed low-preload candidate trial. Compare the two disturbed trials at the same marked preload setting. Record displacement, corner lift, visible seal damage and reopening time. Reject on displacement over 1 mm, failure at 20 N, reopening over 30 seconds, seal tears, obstruction or permanent deformation. This schedule has not been demonstrated feasible within the observation allowance.
assumptions: Accessible rim geometry supports strip-pair capture and lateral bearing with the supplied strip and bolt dimensions; this is indispensable and unknown.
Balanced preload may still cause rocking; rubber-pad compliance and bearing capacity are unmeasured.
Fast release and safe tether parking are unproven.

assessment: A prototype question, not deployment approval. Missing rim geometry can defeat fabrication before testing; no relaxation of hard constraints or additional equipment is assumed. A successful candidate result would support this fixture only, and preload differences could confound the rival comparison.
